generation.explanation: The sine graph is wavy because it is really circular motion viewed from the side. sin(θ) is just the vertical height of a point traveling around the unit circle: as the angle θ grows, that height climbs smoothly to 1, slides back through 0, dips to −1, and returns to 0. Every full turn repeats this same rise-and-fall, so the graph becomes an endless, smooth wave with period 2π. In the visualization, watch the yellow dot ride around the circle while its height is 'unwrapped' onto the graph — the wave is born from spinning.
